I have farmed cotton in Quzhou County for forty years, and at 65 I know every mu of my 12 mu plot. With only my wife and me in the household, cotton is the right crop—it is what our well-irrigated land suits best, and it gives us a stable cash income. I will plant an improved variety such as Guoxinmian or 99-1, because these seeds give consistent germination and higher lint yield than the old traditional types. In late March I will do rotary tillage to break up the soil and prepare a fine seedbed, then sow in mid-April when the soil temperature is steady. For fertilizer, I will spread compound fertilizer at sowing and add a urea topdressing at flowering time. I will irrigate three times through the season—at flowering, at boll setting, and once in August if the weather turns dry—because my well gives reliable water. Pests are the biggest worry: bollworm, aphids and red spider mite are common here, so I spray insecticide roughly every ten days from June to September, plus one herbicide application before sowing. I expect about 580 kg of seed cotton per mu if the weather cooperates.
